title: Computer Vision Engineer Roadmap
summary: Build programming, mathematics and machine-learning foundations first, then specialise in image processing, deep learning, vision transformers and production computer-vision systems.

facts.Current degree: B.Tech / B.E. — CSE - Artificial Intelligence & Machine Learning
facts.Timeline assumption: This roadmap assumes a four-year B.Tech/B.E. programme beginning in 2026 and progressing through 2030.

rows.text: 3 Python programs + 50 programming problems + GitHub repo with README
Linear algebra, calculus, probability, statistics, NumPy
Implement 10 numerical/statistical operations and explain them
DSA, SQL, pandas, image arrays and data handling
100 DSA problems + reproducible image/data preprocessing notebook
Image processing, filtering, edges, features, segmentation
Build 3 image-processing pipelines and document failure cases
CNNs, transfer learning, object detection, segmentation
Train a CNN and an object-detection/segmentation model; report precision/recall and errors
Vision transformers, multimodal AI, model serving, internship/open source
Deploy one vision model as an API with documented latency and evaluation
MLOps, Docker, cloud, monitoring and efficient inference
Containerised vision service + automated deployment + monitoring
Portfolio, system design, research and interviews
3 substantial vision projects + architecture diagrams + 5 mock interviews

blocks.text: Use the additional year for advanced vision research, a substantial industry project, publication-quality experiments, robotics/edge-AI work or open-source contributions. The BCA-specific 3-year/4-year credit figures do not apply to this B.Tech/B.E. roadmap.

rows.text: Image processing, OCR, NLP, layout understanding
OpenCV, geometry, depth, robotics, sensor fusion
Model optimisation, ONNX, inference, embedded systems

blocks.text: Move from training individual vision models to designing complete perception systems. Develop expertise in multimodal AI, efficient inference, edge deployment, sensor fusion, evaluation, safety and system architecture while retaining strong mathematics and software-engineering fundamentals.

Long-term computer-vision engineering increasingly involves complete perception systems rather than isolated models. Build expertise in multimodal models, 3D perception, sensor fusion, edge inference, model efficiency, evaluation, safety and system architecture while retaining strong mathematics and software-engineering foundations.
